newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh coal miners protest over pension reform.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh coal miners protest over pension reform.

text.p: Hundreds of coal miners in the Kazakh rust-belt town of Karaganda held a rare unsanctioned demonstration on Monday in protest over pension reforms in the ex-Soviet state, a union official said.

"Today, from 10.00 am to 11.00 am (0300 to 0400 GMT) a demonstration took place in Karaganda at which about 500 people took part," Leonid Martynov, deputy chairman of the Republican Federation of Trade Unions, told Reuters in the capital Almaty.
Police in Karaganda confirmed by telephone that an unsanctioned protest had taken place.

Market economic reforms have brought great hardship to much of the 16.9 million population but there are few protests in the republic where President Nursultan Nazarbayev enjoys strong executive powers and tolerates little dissent.
"The demonstrators were not allowed to proceed to the square in front of the regional administration, which was surrounded by police," Martynov said.
He said miners were angered over Kazakh government pension reform, which he said would see "no privileges for the miners".
The government has said it plans to move away from state-run pension funds to private ones.

Elderly people were also among the demonstrators, Martynov said, demanding months of unpaid pensions. The government owes around 36 billion tenge ($480 million) to pensioners which it has vowed to pay off by the end of the year.
